CONTENT PREVIEW:
Feature: Add Go formatting check with gofumpt to CI

# GitHub Issue #147: Add Go formatting check with gofumpt to CI pipeline

**Category**: code quality | **Scope**: Small

**Description**: There is no Go formatting check in the CI pipeline. `gofumpt` is a strict superset of `gofmt` that enforces additional formatting rules widely adopted in the Go community. A dedicated CI job should verify that all Go source files conform to `gofumpt` formatting and fail the pipeline if unformatted code is detected.

Proposed CI job:

```yaml
format-check:
  needs: [changes]
  if: needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true'
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  timeout-minutes: 5
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
      with:
        go-version-file: go.work
    - run: |
        go install mvdan.cc/gofumpt@latest
        test -z "$(gofumpt -l .)" || { gofumpt -d .; exit 1; }
```

**Motivation**: Without an enforced formatting standard in CI, formatting inconsistencies accumulate over time and pollute diffs with whitespace-only changes, making code review harder. `gofumpt` goes beyond `gofmt` by enforcing stricter rules (e.g. removing unnecessary blank lines, grouping imports consistently) that reduce stylistic debates in reviews. Catching formatting issues in CI prevents them from reaching the main branch and ensures all contributors produce consistently formatted code regardless of their local editor setup.

**Affected Areas**:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`
- Go source f

<subject-line>
  <rule name="format">"plan(CC-0053): <short description>"</rule>
  <rule name="types">feat | fix | test | refactor | docs | style | chore</rule>
  <rule name="length">Max 50 chars recommended, 72 chars absolute maximum</rule>
  <rule name="style">Imperative mood ("add" not "added", "fix" not "fixed")</rule>
  <rule name="punctuation">No period at end, capitalize after colon</rule>
</subject-line>

<body optional="true">
  <rule>Blank line required between subject and body</rule>
  <rule>Wrap lines at 72 characters maximum</rule>
  <rule>Explain WHAT changed and WHY (not HOW)</rule>
</body>

<avoid>
  <rule>Include "WIP", "temp", "test", or placeholder text</rule>
  <rule>Commit unrelated changes in the same commit</rule>
  <rule>Use past tense ("added", "fixed", "changed")</rule>
  <rule>Include issue numbers without context</rule>
</avoid>

<never-stage>
  NEVER stage or commit build/runtime artifacts. Before running `git add`,
  verify that NONE of these are included:
  - Python: __pycache__/, *.pyc, *.pyo, .venv/, venv/, .mypy_cache/,
    .ruff_cache/, .pytest_cache/, *.egg-info/, dist/, build/, .tox/, .nox/
  - Node.js: node_modules/, .next/, .turbo/, .parcel-cache/
  - Rust: target/, *.rlib
  - Go: *.test binary outputs
  - Compiled: *.exe, *.dll, *.so, *.dylib, *.o, *.obj, *.a, *.wasm
  - JVM: *.class, *.jar, *.war, *.ear
  - .NET: bin/, obj/, *.nupkg
  - Terraform: .terraform/, *.tfstate
  - OS: .DS_Store, Thumbs.db
  Use `git add <specific-files>` instead of `git add .` or `git add -A`.
  If in doubt, run `git status` first and only stage source files.
</never-stage>
</commit-best-practices>
